body: We had a requirement to compare the two HTTP Requests, so we used the **queryEquals** method.
Ok, why not `equals`? Did you change the visibility of `queryEquals`, or were using `equalType`?
We are using equalType(). The reason of using it over equals() is, the way of comparison in the former. It uses Set to hold the url/body parameters.
Ok if there's a use case we can leave it in and fix it.
Agreed, although we need to document the method a lot better (i.e. it's also checking the body, but not always just the parameter names, sometimes it might include the "values").
Ok I'll try to update the PR at lunchtime, failing that I'll tackle it later tonight.
When would it include values? It uses `getParamNameSet(Type)` which builds the name set from the key of a name value pair map.
Basically anything that's not `x-www-form-urlencoded`, that can be reproduced easily with a JSON payload.
Ok the PR now includes some javadoc content which attempts to address such situations.
